claim: zxing-cpp (pip install zxing-cpp, Apache-2.0) decodes GS1 DataMatrix rendered by BWIPP/treepoem (with Ghostscript) on Windows and reports content_type GS1 so that AI (01)(17)(10)(21) can be parsed.
evidence: DECODER SIDE (empirically verified on this Windows 11 machine, Python 3.12, zxing-cpp 3.1.1 from PyPI, license expression Apache-2.0): zxingcpp.ContentType exposes ['Text','Binary','Mixed','GS1','ISO15434','UnknownECI']; read_barcodes() defaults to text_mode=TextMode.HRI. Round trip of a GS1 DataMatrix created with zxingcpp.create_barcode(data, BarcodeFormat.DataMatrix, gs1=True) for '(01)09521234543213(17)261231(10)ABC123(21)XYZ789' decoded to content_type=ContentType.GS1, symbology_identifier=']d2', text='(01)09521234543213(17)261231(10)ABC123(21)XYZ789', bytes=b'01095212345432131726123110ABC123\x1d21XYZ789'. Source confirms mechanism: datamatrix/DMDecoder.cpp sets symbology.modifier='2' when FNC1 is at the first codeword position, aiFlag=AIFlag::GS1, and translates later FNC1 to ASCII 29 <GS>; Content.cpp returns ContentType::GS1 when aiFlag==GS1 and renders HRI via HRIFromGS1 (HRI.cpp wraps AIs in parentheses using a fixed/variable-length AI table; returns empty and falls back to escaped text if an AI prefix is unknown). A control symbol written WITHOUT gs1=True decoded as ContentType.Text / ']d1', showing the GS1 flag depends purely on the leading FNC1, i.e. on the encoder emitting it. ENCODER SIDE (documentation only; Ghostscript is NOT installed on this machine so the BWIPP render itself could not be executed): BWIPP wiki 'GS1 DataMatrix' states input is in GS1 AI standard format e.g. '(01)09521234543213(17)120508(10)ABCD1234(410)9501101020917' and 'it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary'. treepoem (installed from PyPI, MIT) lists 'gs1datamatrix' in treepoem.barcode_types; its README says 'You'll also need Ghostscript installed'; its source _ghostscript_binary() searches ('gswin32c','gswin64c','gs') on Windows and uses CREATE_NO_WINDOW, so Windows is supported given a Ghostscript install (gswin64c.exe on PATH). The GitHub README offered as support does not itself mention GS1 or content_type; the API facts come from wrappers/python/zxing.cpp and core sources.
correction: zxing-cpp 3.1.1 (pip install zxing-cpp, Apache-2.0) decodes GS1 DataMatrix (FNC1 in first position) and reports content_type == ContentType.GS1 with symbology_identifier ']d2'; with the default text_mode=HRI, result.text is already '(01)...(17)...(10)...(21)...' and result.bytes holds the raw element string with ASCII 29 GS separators. This was verified live on Windows using zxing-cpp's own GS1 writer; the BWIPP/treepoem 'gs1datamatrix' render was verified only from documentation (BWIPP inserts FNC1 automatically; treepoem finds gswin64c on Windows) because Ghostscript was not installed here, so the exact end-to-end BWIPP->zxing round trip on Windows remains to be executed once. Caveats: (a) the GS1 flag is set solely by the leading FNC1, so use treepoem barcode_type='gs1datamatrix' (not 'datamatrix' with parsed ^FNC1) to be safe; (b) BWIPP lints AI syntax by default, so invalid (17) dates or GTIN check digits raise errors unless dontlint is passed; (c) HRI rendering falls back to escaped raw text when an AI is unknown to zxing's table, so parse AIs from result.bytes (split on \x1d) rather than relying on the HRI string; (d) the referenced GitHub README does not document content_type/GS1 — cite wrappers/python/zxing.cpp and Content.cpp instead; (e) Ghostscript (AGPL) must be installed separately and gswin64c.exe must be on PATH.
impact_on_candidate: Low risk. The free-tool round trip is viable: the decoder half is empirically proven on Windows and the encoder half is standard BWIPP behavior. Residual action for the team is a 5-minute smoke test after installing Ghostscript (treepoem.generate_barcode('gs1datamatrix', '(01)...(17)...(10)...(21)...') -> zxingcpp.read_barcodes -> assert content_type == GS1). If that single test failed, the fallback is zxing-cpp's own create_barcode(..., gs1=True) writer (already verified here), which removes the Ghostscript dependency entirely, so a switch to bwip-js/pylibdmtx is not needed. UDI AIDC checks and barcode-change detection in redlines should parse from result.bytes (GS-separated) with a GS1 AI table rather than from the HRI text.
